While methods such as SAUCIE, LIGER, BBKNN and Seurat v3 tend to favor the removal of batch effects over conservation of biological variation, DESC and Conos make the opposite choice, and Scanorama, scVI and FastMNN (gene) balance these two objectives. Other methods strike different balances per task (Extended Data Fig. 4). This tradeoff is particularly noticeable where biological and batch effects overlap. For example, in the lung task, three datasets sample two distinct spatial locations (airway and parenchyma). Particular cell types such as endothelial cells perform different functions in these loca - tions (for example, gas exchange in the parenchyma).
